name: Plasmodium vivax

taxonomy.rank_note: Reference groups can include multiple species. Protozoan higher-rank systems differ; the lineage is provided without forcing every clade into a class rank.

morphology: Infected erythrocytes often enlarge and show Schüffner stippling; trophozoites may be amoeboid. Mature schizonts commonly contain 12–24 merozoites.
These are blood stages, not eggs; erythrocyte context is essential, and crop pixels do not establish biological size.

transmission.detail: Anopheles inoculates sporozoites, followed by liver development and erythrocytic replication; gametocytes infect mosquitoes, where sexual reproduction occurs. Liver hypnozoites may persist.

life_cycle.detail: Anopheles inoculates sporozoites, followed by liver development and erythrocytic replication; gametocytes infect mosquitoes, where sexual reproduction occurs. Liver hypnozoites may persist.
Asexual parasites and gametocytes in peripheral blood; thick and thin films serve different purposes.

hosts: Definitive: Anopheles mosquito. Intermediate: humans; macaques are important reservoirs for P. knowlesi.
distribution: Focal distribution: falciparum and vivax malaria are especially relevant to Thai border/forest exposure; other species may be uncommon or imported. Ovale malaria is particularly associated with sub-Saharan African exposure.
clinical_significance: Febrile malaria and anemia; dormant liver hypnozoites can cause relapses, and severe illness can occur.
specimen: Asexual parasites and gametocytes in peripheral blood; thick and thin films serve different purposes.
diagnostics: Giemsa thick films support detection; thin films preserve erythrocytes for identification, typically at 1000× oil immersion.
Rapid diagnostic tests complement microscopy; molecular assays resolve difficult species identifications.
differential_diagnosis: P. ovale also enlarges and stipples cells; evaluate whole erythrocytes and multiple stages.
review_status: Source-compiled educational content; not independently clinically validated

annotation_guidance: Record specimen, stage, stain, objective/total magnification, pixel calibration, source image and reviewer certainty.
Native crops of 200–650 pixels do not determine biological size. Retain µm-per-pixel calibration before resizing.
Split training, validation and test data by patient/specimen; keep related crops in the same split.
Keep damaged or ambiguous objects uncertain. Molecular confirmation of a mixed specimen does not assign every pictured object a species.
Separate thick and thin films; retain erythrocyte context for malaria and full head/tail context for microfilariae.
